root.name: root
root.definition: The head of the sentence. It depends on nothing else; every other word is connected to it through a chain of relations.

nsubj.name: nominal subject
nsubj.definition: A nominal that is the syntactic subject of a clause. In English it is usually the noun phrase before the verb that agrees with it ("The child is eating").

nsubj:pass.name: passive nominal subject
nsubj:pass.definition: The subject of a passive clause: the nominal that would be the object in the corresponding active clause ("The letter was written").

nsubj:outer.name: outer clause nominal subject
nsubj:outer.definition: The nominal subject of a copular clause whose predicate is itself a clause; the label signals that it is not the subject of that nested clause ("The problem is that we left").

csubj:outer.name: outer clause clausal subject
csubj:outer.definition: A clausal subject of a copular clause whose predicate is itself a clause.

obj.name: object
obj.definition: The nominal that is the direct object of a verb: typically the entity most directly affected by the event ("eating rice").

iobj.name: indirect object
iobj.definition: A second, unmarked nominal object of a verb, typically the recipient ("She gave her brother a book").

csubj.name: clausal subject
csubj.definition: A clause that functions as the subject of another clause ("What she said surprised me").

csubj:pass.name: clausal passive subject
csubj:pass.definition: A clause that is the subject of a passive clause ("That he lied was suspected").

ccomp.name: clausal complement
ccomp.definition: A clause that is a core argument of a verb or adjective, with its own subject, functioning like an object ("She said that he left").

xcomp.name: open clausal complement
xcomp.definition: A predicative complement without its own subject; its subject is understood from an argument of the higher clause ("She wants to leave", "They consider him smart").

obl.name: oblique nominal
obl.definition: A nominal that is a non-core (oblique) argument or adjunct of a predicate, often marked by a preposition ("She saw it with a telescope", "He left on Monday").

obl:agent.name: agent in a passive
obl:agent.definition: The oblique phrase expressing the agent of a passive clause, in English introduced by "by" ("written by Mary").

obl:unmarked.name: adpositionless oblique
obl:unmarked.definition: An oblique that is a bare nominal with no preposition, e.g. many time and measure expressions ("I left yesterday", "They live two miles away").

obl:tmod.name: temporal modifier (older label)
obl:tmod.definition: A bare nominal expressing time that modifies a predicate ("I left yesterday"). Recent UD English releases use obl:unmarked for this.

vocative.name: vocative
vocative.definition: A nominal used to address the listener directly ("Mary, come here").

expl.name: expletive
expl.definition: A pronoun that fills a syntactic argument position but carries no meaning, such as English "there" in "There is a problem" or "it" in "It is raining".

dislocated.name: dislocated element
dislocated.definition: A fronted or postposed element that does not fill a regular grammatical role but is coreferent with one ("This book, I really liked it").

advcl.name: adverbial clause modifier
advcl.definition: A clause that modifies a predicate like an adverb, expressing time, cause, condition, purpose and similar notions ("She left because she was tired").

advcl:relcl.name: adverbial relative clause modifier
advcl:relcl.definition: A relative clause that is adverbial, for example one that modifies a whole clause rather than a nominal ("She passed, which surprised everyone").

advmod.name: adverbial modifier
advmod.definition: An adverb or adverbial phrase that modifies a predicate or a modifier word ("ran quickly", "very tall", "not").

discourse.name: discourse element
discourse.definition: An interjection or discourse particle that is not clearly linked to the structure of the sentence ("well", "um", emoticons).

aux.name: auxiliary
aux.definition: A function word attached to a predicate that expresses tense, mood, aspect, voice or evidentiality ("is eating", "will go", "has eaten").

aux:pass.name: passive auxiliary
aux:pass.definition: The auxiliary that marks passive voice ("was written", "got arrested").

cop.name: copula
cop.definition: The function word linking a subject to a non-verbal predicate ("She is a teacher"). In UD the non-verbal predicate, not the copula, is the head of the clause.

mark.name: marker
mark.definition: A function word that introduces a subordinate clause, such as a subordinating conjunction or infinitival "to" ("because she was tired", "to leave").

nmod.name: nominal modifier
nmod.definition: A nominal that modifies another nominal, usually marked by a preposition or case ("the man with a telescope", "the roof of the house").

nmod:poss.name: possessive nominal modifier
nmod:poss.definition: A possessor modifying a nominal ("her book", "Mary's car").

nmod:unmarked.name: adpositionless nominal modifier
nmod:unmarked.definition: A bare nominal (no preposition or possessive marking) that modifies another nominal.

nmod:desc.name: descriptor modifier
nmod:desc.definition: A bare nominal descriptor occurring in or with a name, such as a title or description that is neither prepositional nor possessive.

nmod:tmod.name: temporal nominal modifier (older label)
nmod:tmod.definition: A bare temporal nominal modifying another nominal ("the meeting yesterday"). Recent UD English releases use nmod:unmarked for this.

appos.name: appositional modifier
appos.definition: A nominal placed next to another nominal that renames or describes the same referent ("Sam, my brother, arrived").

nummod.name: numeric modifier
nummod.definition: A number that modifies a noun to express quantity ("three books").

acl.name: adnominal clause
acl.definition: A clause that modifies a nominal, such as a participial or infinitival clause ("the man sitting there", "a book to read").

acl:relcl.name: relative clause modifier
acl:relcl.definition: A relative clause modifying a nominal ("the book that the professor recommended").

amod.name: adjectival modifier
amod.definition: An adjective or adjectival phrase that modifies a nominal ("red car").

det.name: determiner
det.definition: A determiner attached to a nominal: articles, demonstratives, quantifiers ("the child", "this book").

det:predet.name: predeterminer
det:predet.definition: A word that precedes the determiner in a noun phrase ("all the students").

clf.name: classifier
clf.definition: A word that accompanies a numeral or determiner and classifies the noun; common in languages such as Chinese or Japanese, not used in English.

case.name: case marking
case.definition: A preposition, postposition or case particle attached to the nominal it marks. In UD the preposition depends on the noun ("with → telescope"), not the other way round.

conj.name: conjunct
conj.definition: A non-first element of a coordination, attached to the first conjunct ("cats and dogs": dogs → cats).

cc.name: coordinating conjunction
cc.definition: The conjunction of a coordination, attached to the following conjunct.

cc:preconj.name: preconjunct
cc:preconj.definition: The first part of a paired conjunction ("either ... or", "both ... and").

fixed.name: fixed multiword expression
fixed.definition: Links the words of a grammaticalized multiword expression that acts as a single function word ("because of", "as well as").

flat.name: flat expression
flat.definition: Links the parts of an expression without a clear internal head, such as names and dates ("Hillary Rodham Clinton").

compound.name: compound
compound.definition: Links the parts of a compound word or noun-noun compound ("phone book", "ice cream").

compound:prt.name: phrasal verb particle
compound:prt.definition: The particle of a phrasal verb ("pick up", "give in").

list.name: list
list.definition: Links items of a list-like sequence that are not coordinated with a conjunction.

parataxis.name: parataxis
parataxis.definition: Links clauses placed side by side without an explicit coordinator or subordinator, such as reported-speech tags or clauses joined by a colon ("The guy, John said, left").

orphan.name: orphan
orphan.definition: Used in ellipsis, when the head of a clause is missing, to connect the remaining dependents ("Mary won gold and Peter bronze").

goeswith.name: goes with
goeswith.definition: Links parts of a word that were wrongly split in the text ("other wise").

reparandum.name: overridden disfluency
reparandum.definition: Links a speech disfluency to its correction ("go to the right- to the left").

punct.name: punctuation
punct.definition: Attaches a punctuation mark to the head of the clause or phrase it belongs to.

dep.name: unspecified dependency
dep.definition: A dependency the annotation (or parser) could not classify more precisely.
